- Subprocessor onshore processing: We do not proactively route customer production PII to APAC-based subprocessors unless a customer requests it and signs an addendum specifying the routing and any additional safeguards. We can do a carve-out in the Transfer Annex for Mercury.
- Annotated dataflow: attaching a first pass (see 20260914-dataflow-annotated-v2.png) that flags cleartext PII, hashed/pseudonymized identifiers, and telemetry.
- Audit logs & KMS: Redwood retains token-access audit logs for 18 months by default; we can commit 12 months in the annex. KMS custody for hosted customers is Redwood-managed keys (we can also support customer-managed keys via KMS). See the draft DTA in Drive (link below).

Next steps I propose:
1) Kimberly and Grace from our privacy/security ops will review the annotated flow and confirm whether any runtime component would need onshore subprocessor access to satisfy Mercury's use cases.
2) We'll produce a short appendix describing the onshore carve-out language and a subprocessor list export (CSV).
3) If that looks good, we can circulate a DTA addendum for signature (DocuSign).

Kim / Rishi / Alice — thanks for the detailed ask. Quick confirmations and the next deliverables below.

- Data categories: confirmed. The attached annotated PNG marks fields as PII / pseudonymized / telemetry. We flagged SSN as a high-risk field and recommend redaction before any subprocessor export.
- Pseudonymization: runtime proxy pseudonymizes identifiers at ingress; de-identified tokens are used for inference and are not reversible without customer KMS keys. Downstream analytics systems receive hashed tokens only.
- Onshore subprocessors: currently, two support partners have APAC presence (PartnerA APAC Ltd., PartnerB Pty). They do not process unredacted customer PII for hosted production by default. They may access pseudonymized identifiers for operational debugging under RBAC and with a documented escalation. We will add explicit language to the Transfer Annex to require customer opt-in for any cleartext processing onshore.
- Routing controls: yes — we have a routing policy flag ("apac_onshore_processing_allowed") we can gate behind the addendum. I included suggested policy text in the Drive doc.
- Audit logs: default retention 18 months; commit 12 months in the annex. We can export a compressed evidentiary bundle (logs + supporting traces) on 30 day SLA for procurement/audit requests.
- KMS custody: we support Redwood-managed KMS (default), customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own) via AWS KMS / GCP KMS integrations, and HSM-backed key custody for enterprise private deployments. Key rotation and sync windows are documented in the Security Appendix (link).

Deliverables attached/shared:
- subprocessor-roster-202609.csv (attached)
- Mercury-DTA-draft.docx (Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/mercury/dpa-annotated-dataflow)
- annotated diagram: 20260914-dataflow-annotated-v2.png

Alice — please confirm if the addendum approach and the 12-month audit retention commitment are acceptable. If yes, Rishi, can you push the DTA addendum through DocuSign Friday?

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
